bibliographic.title: Conversational AI for perinatal mental health: promise, limits, and a human-AI stepped-care framework
bibliographic.citation_apa: Yang, H., & Lin, D.-M. (2026). Conversational AI for perinatal mental health: promise, limits, and a human-AI stepped-care framework. Frontiers in Psychiatry, 17, 1847854. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2026.1847854

methodology.study_design: conceptual framework paper with literature-informed argumentation
methodology.technology_context: conversational AI, digital doulas, generative AI, large language models, chatbots, multimodal interaction, NLP-based mental health support

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article directly addresses conversational AI and large language models in a high-stakes regulated healthcare domain (perinatal mental health), and proposes a human-AI stepped-care framework emphasizing human oversight, escalation protocols, medico-legal accountability, safety-by-design, and equity-centered evaluation.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial full-text excerpts were provided (approximately pages 1-6); complete manuscript review needed to confirm absence of empirical components and to verify full governance discussion.

appraisal.notes: Appropriate as a conceptual governance-oriented perspective for regulated conversational AI, but not an empirical study; sampling and data-collection criteria are largely not applicable. Rigor rests on cited literature and normative argument rather than primary data.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is internally coherent and highly relevant to conversational governance in regulated healthcare, but confidence is moderated because the work is conceptual, not empirically validated, and the appraisal is based on partial text.

coding.theme: Human-AI stepped-care governance for conversational AI in perinatal mental health
coding.subtheme: Safety-by-design with mandatory escalation and non-substitution of human care
concepts: four core functions (companionship, symptom interpretation, navigation, sentinel monitoring)

synthesis.main_claim: Digital doulas should be framed as AI-enabled relational interfaces embedded within a stepped-care model rather than autonomous substitutes for clinicians, with safety-by-design emphasizing human oversight, escalation protocols, workflow integration, and equity-centered evaluation.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes four core functions for digital doulas (companionship, symptom interpretation, navigation, sentinel monitoring) and a safety-by-design agenda for governed deployment of conversational AI/LLMs in perinatal mental health, including deterministic crisis overrides and differentiated human-on-the-loop versus human-in-the-loop oversight.
synthesis.limitations: Conceptual argument without reported primary empirical evaluation; risks discussed include illusion of empathy, crisis recognition failure, algorithmic bias, privacy vulnerabilities, and unsafe deployment.
synthesis.use_in_review: High-value central conceptual evidence for conversational governance in regulated healthcare, especially human oversight tiers, escalation/handoff design, guardrails, accountability, and equity risks in LLM-based conversational systems.

evidence.claim: Article is peer-reviewed journal publication in Frontiers in Psychiatry
evidence.excerpt: REVIEWED BY Jasmine Joseph, CHRIST (Deemed to be University), India

evidence.claim: Study is conceptual framework, not empirical primary research
evidence.excerpt: We propose four core functions for digital doulas: companionship, symptom interpretation, navigation, and sentinel monitoring.

evidence.claim: Direct relevance to LLMs and generative AI in conversational mental health care
evidence.excerpt: generative AI and large language models are rapidly entering mental health care.
Perinatal mental health conditions are highly prevalent, clinically consequential, and persistently undertreated.

evidence.claim: Human oversight and escalation governance proposed
evidence.excerpt: we outline a safety-by-design agenda emphasizing human oversight, clear escalation protocols with medico-legal accountability

evidence.claim: Differentiated oversight model: human-on-the-loop vs human-in-the-loop
evidence.excerpt: routine monitoring, which may operate with human-on-the-loop oversight (periodic clinician review), and crisis escalation, which requires mandatory human-in-the-loop real-time engagement

evidence.claim: Operational guardrail example with deterministic override bypassing generative layer
evidence.excerpt: When the model detects specific keywords related to self-harm or infant harm, it completely bypasses the generative AI layer, halting open-ended conversation and immediately triggering deterministic crisis escalation pathways

evidence.claim: Identifies LLM-specific conversational risk: algorithmic sycophancy
evidence.excerpt: A unique danger of large language models in this context is "algorithmic sycophancy"—the tendency of models trained on human feedback to be overly agreeable and validating.

evidence.claim: Crisis recognition and escalation pathway failures in conversational agents
evidence.excerpt: they still frequently fail to provide reliable source citations or actionable emergency escalation pathways

evidence.claim: Equity and bias concerns in NLP/conversational deployment
evidence.excerpt: Eurocentric Natural Language Processing (NLP) models often fail to recognize diverse "cultural idioms of distress."

evidence.claim: Authors position AI as adjunct, not replacement, supporting governance of substitution risk
evidence.excerpt: digital doulas should not be framed as autonomous substitutes for clinicians or human doulas

evidence.claim: Privacy and data governance risks acknowledged
evidence.excerpt: data privacy vulnerabilities, and unsafe deployment

evidence.claim: Generative AI used only for manuscript language editing, not scientific content generation
evidence.excerpt: generative AI was used in the creation of this manuscript. For language editing and polishing only
